headline: Fed week opens with all 100 Reuters-polled economists expecting a December hike as oil stokes inflation fears
subhead: The S&P 500 fell 0.5 percent Friday and the Nifty 50 sits 1.7 percent above its 52-week low, with the Fed on Wednesday, Microsoft and Alphabet that evening and Amazon on Thursday.

us.text: The S&P 500 fell 0.5 percent to 7,623.7 and the Dow 1.2 percent Friday as Brent settled at 116.72 dollars, reviving oil-driven inflation fears.
A Reuters poll found 94 of 100 economists expect the Fed to hold at 3.75 to 4.00 percent Wednesday, and all 100 expect a December hike.
Big Tech earnings test AI spending this week: Microsoft and Alphabet report after Wednesday's close and Amazon after Thursday's.

india.text: The Nifty 50 fell 0.4 percent to 22,600 Friday, a fourth straight loss leaving it 1.7 percent above its 52-week low; Bank Nifty lost 1.2 percent.
Provisional data showed FIIs net bought 887.65 crore rupees and DIIs 3,235.36 crore rupees of cash equities on Friday.
The rupee fell 12 paise to 94.93 per dollar, pressured by rising crude prices and weak domestic equities.

global.text: The Hang Seng rose 0.7 percent to 23,093.4 Friday as tech and EV shares recovered from Thursday's regulatory-driven selloff.
The FTSE 100 slipped 0.3 percent to 10,690.4 and the DAX 0.8 percent to 25,181.7 as oil replaced AI as the main worry.
Bitcoin hit 79,146 dollars Saturday as over 810 million dollars of positions were liquidated; it trades at 80,151, down 0.8 percent.

weekly.narrative: Two forces ran the week and both pointed at the cost of capital. Attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, including Iranian claims that seven vessels were hit or mined, took Brent above 117 dollars and WTI past 100, and because that lands as an inflation shock rather than a growth scare it lifted rate expectations instead of safe havens: gold fell 4.3 percent on the week to within about 1.0 percent of its 52 week low and silver hit a year to date low, while the US 10 year held near 4.99 percent. The second force was the AI financing question, which moved from equity multiples to credit, with a Lam Research warning on chip supply into 2027 knocking the Nasdaq 2.6 percent on Thursday, CoreWeave 2032 bonds quoted near 78 cents on the dollar, and Jensen Huang arguing the sector is short of capital rather than demand. India inverted the pattern, with the Nifty pressured by the oil bill and foreign selling while IT rallied on a reverse AI trade that reads weaker AI capex as work returning to traditional services firms, and the rupee closed at 94.93 against the dollar. Next week stacks the catalysts: the Fed decision on 28 October with a hike priced near 7.6 percent, Microsoft and Alphabet that same evening, Amazon plus Q3 GDP and September PCE on 29 October, the Bank of Japan on 30 October, and in Mumbai the listing of the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms issue alongside five new mainboard IPOs.
